PullRequest.Title: chat: Fix customization list corners, detail scrollbars, and row color
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #335856 Fixes #335857 Before: Not styled - ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/121c4cb6-65e2-4c39-92bf-5b5187a52751) ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f10a2b37-94e5-4ef1-be08-f34207f2d8ed) After: ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0549de72-9dac-4af5-b276-f750db6d1c35) ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b8b4574d-d729-450e-a625-fe7b965cd47c) ## Summary - keep grouped AI Customizations inventories rounded as a whole while rendering interior rows with flat corners across Plugins, MCP Servers, Agents, Skills, Instructions, Hooks, and Prompts - wrap the Plugins detail body in `DomScrollableElement` so the page uses the product's themed vertical scrollbar and remains scrollable as its content changes - rescan the detail scrollbar after resize, synchronous content updates, and asynchronous README rendering - theme overflowing README code-block scrollbars with the standard scrollbar tokens, pill-shaped thumbs, and hover/active states ## Validation - `npm run compile` - ESLint on the changed TypeScript files - stylelint on `aiCustomizationManagement.css` - focused AI Customizations management editor tests: 29 passing - narrow live-product verification of vertical detail scrolling and visible horizontal README overflow - `git diff --check` `npm run hygiene` was attempted but the Windows runner failed before source checks because it resolved `remote/package.json` as `Q:\Q:\vscode.worktrees\fix-extension-tools-scrollbar-issue\remote\package.json`. The targeted ESLint and stylelint checks pass. ## Row background Customization rows now inherit the page background at rest, matching the Plugins page while retaining themed hover feedback and grouped borders.
Before After

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an installed plugin detail and render its README
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The detail shell and metadata render synchronously; the existing README filesystem read completes before README markdown appears, but does not block opening the detail shell. After content insertion, the new scrollbar geometry scan runs synchronously to make the rendered body scrollable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the installed plugin's README.md through IFileService.readFile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per selected installed plugin detail; no loop or collection fan-out is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same README file read occurred once per selected plugin before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial shell-render critical path but required before README content is displayed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: README DOM size, including rendered code blocks and images; one scrollbar scan follows initial insertion, one aggregate callback follows asynchronous code-block rendering, and image loads can each trigger a scan.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A selected README is loaded asynchronously. Rapid selections can leave prior reads in flight because CancellationToken.None is pre-existing; generation guards prevent stale rendering. The diff adds no new I/O concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No explicit README cache or request coalescing exists in this component before or after the diff; warm behavior depends on the underlying file service/OS cache. The diff does not alter keys, misses, or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path, single-read cardinality, asynchronous rendering callbacks, and synchronous geometry reads.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large READMEs can make geometry reads more expensive, but scans are tied to actual content completion/load events and are necessary for scroll dimensions; no realistic diff-introduced multiplicity establishes a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded layout synchronization for the new scrollbar without increasing README I/O or moving it onto the initial detail-shell critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a marketplace plugin detail with a remote README
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The detail shell renders immediately; the existing HTTPS GET must complete before the README is parsed and displayed. New scrollbar scanning occurs only after synchronous metadata changes and remote content/render completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch a marketplace README with IRequestService.request and decode the response text.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One GET per selected marketplace plugin with an HTTPS README URI; no per-section, per-code-block, or per-image network request is added by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single GET and response decoding occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for remote README display but not for showing the plugin detail shell.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Remote README response size controls existing network, decode, markdown, and DOM cost; the diff adds only bounded scrollbar scans after content changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One request is started per selection, with possible overlap across rapid selections due to pre-existing uncancelled requests; the diff does not add or amplify concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No component-level cache or coalescing exists before or after the diff. Any warm-cache behavior is delegated to the request stack; unsupported/missing README behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the direct showEmbeddedPluginDetail -> setInput -> renderReadme -> loadPluginReadme path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote latency and README size vary, but the unchanged boundary dominates and the new scan count does not scale with response chunks or collection cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression because the network boundary, cardinality, cache behavior, and scheduling are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize, keyboard-scroll, or dynamically reflow an open plugin detail
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ResizeObserver callbacks and content-change events synchronously call DomScrollableElement.scanDomNode, which reads client/scroll dimensions and updates scrollbar state. Keyboard navigation performs constant-time dimension reads and one scroll-position update per handled key event.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with actual editor resize notifications, narrow-layout threshold transitions, asynchronous markdown completion, image load events, or user key events, not with the number of plugins in the inventory.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser ResizeObserver delivery is frame-coalesced; narrow-layout class changes are scheduled for the next animation frame. Markdown code blocks invoke one aggregate callback after Promise.all, while image loads notify individually. Work remains on the UI thread but is bounded to actual changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Scroll dimensions are current DOM state and must be refreshed after viewport or content changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from DomScrollableElement.scanDomNode reading six geometry properties and the traced observer/event registrations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A very large README increases browser layout cost, but the changed code does not rescan per row/frame continuously and follows established DomScrollableElement patterns.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The synchronous work is bounded and directly supports scrollbar correctness; there is no demonstrated loop, per-frame polling, or collection-wide repetition.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The browser applies changed border-radius and background CSS while painting visible list rows; no JavaScript, I/O, serialization, or new DOM creation is introduced.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: CSS matching scales with visible inventory-row DOM nodes under the existing plugin list widget; selectors are scoped and do not add descendant traversal work on an interaction loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single browser style/layout pipeline; no queues or asynchronous boundaries are added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Not applicable beyond normal browser style caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that these are paint/style-only changes with unchanged row cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style-recalculation cost is browser-dependent, but the selectors and declarations are simple and scoped.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The fixture optionally delays mocked README reads and asynchronous code rendering, polls for a row before opening it, then waits for rendering before capturing the scroll state. These waits are confined to test execution.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 20 polling attempts at 50 ms when an expected row is absent; the new plugin-detail fixture additionally uses fixed mocked delays for one README and one code block.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mock README and code-block delays are sequential around fixture rendering; no production concurrency changes result.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: In-memory fixture content map; no production cache or real filesystem/network behavior is exercised.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the bounded loop and explicit timeout calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Fixture runtime increases by fixed hundreds of milliseconds for the modified screenshot case, while polling only waits when rows are not yet available.
Scenarios.Verdict: No product performance finding. The bounded test waits intentionally stabilize asynchronous screenshot state and do not affect shipped code.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. Traced plugin-detail opening, existing README filesystem/network boundaries, markdown completion, resize and keyboard paths, list styling, and fixture behavior. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not establish a concrete shipped regression fix requiring blame attribution.
